segments.role: Important for denying Netanyahu 61, mainly through Ra'am's threshold, but slightly negative for a change-led government under the formation model. Any investment here is a leadership decision, not a field call.
segments.who: The segment's 38 Negev Bedouin localities hold 144,860 eligible voters. Turnout was 51% in 2022, and Arab lists took 94% of the vote. Rahat is by far the largest town. About 40,000 voters from unrecognised villages have no polling station in their village and are assigned by tribe to stations 5-65 km from home, according to the Abraham Initiatives.
segments.moves: Ra'am won about 74% of the Negev Arab vote in 2022, and the forecast gives it an {{fc.Raam.pass|x100|f:.0f}}% chance of passing the threshold. Crime and personal safety top Arab voters' concerns, and 77% back an Arab party joining the coalition. Young Arab voters want concrete plans on crime, housing, jobs and discrimination rather than vague talk of partnership. The CEC's vote to disqualify the Joint List and Ra'am was overturned unanimously by the Supreme Court on 2 October.
segments.approach: The change bloc runs no field programme and no branded turnout work here. The atlas publishes no town-level values or ranks for these localities, and the planner never includes Arab localities or polling stations where Arab lists lead. Per 10,000 extra Ra'am votes, the chance of a change-led government moves by about {{mv.Raam.govt|f:+.2f}} points under the formation model, and the chance of denying Netanyahu 61 by about {{mv.Raam.deny|f:+.2f}} points under the seat law. Under the deny-61 objective the segment holds about {{seg.arab_bedouin_south.block_nb__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation, about {{seg.arab_bedouin_south.block_nb__share|x100|f:.0f}}% of that objective's total. Leadership must decide how much weight blocking gets before anything moves. If it decides to support Arab-sector turnout, that support must be independent of the bloc's campaign, transparent and cleared in writing by election counsel. The bloc runs, funds and directs no turnout work here.
segments.message: Any bloc communication that reaches Negev voters should speak to personal safety and fighting crime, to concrete plans on housing, jobs and services, and to respect for Arab citizens' votes.
segments.messenger: The bloc does not recruit, brief or script messengers for Arab-sector turnout work, and any independent group chooses its own. No bloc-run or bloc-branded turnout activity in these towns. A list's own campaign for its own Arab voters, such as the Democrats' Arabic-language campaign, is that list's decision and goes through its election counsel.
segments.avoid: Avoid any change-bloc rhetoric that treats Arab votes or Arab parties as illegitimate, which can depress Arab turnout. Bloc spokespeople should not make Arab turnout a campaign theme or comment on Arab-sector turnout figures, because Likud plans to use the CEC's station turnout releases to rally its base. The bloc runs no election-day transport or other election-day turnout activity here. Election-day transport, gifts and activity near polling stations are regulated, so check with election counsel.
segments.caveat: Arab-sector turnout is a leadership decision with a real trade-off between objectives, set out on the Strategy page. Any support is independent, transparent and cleared by election counsel. In 2019 the CEC chair ruled that a civil-society plan to bus about 15,000 Bedouin voters was politically motivated, and let it proceed only if the group registered as a body active in the elections. Funding or in-kind support for another list's or a civil-society group's turnout work therefore raises Party Financing Law questions and needs written approval from election counsel.

segments.role: A small segment with a pocket of direct change-list votes, mostly for the Democrats. Turnout here mainly adds Joint List votes, which help deny Netanyahu 61 but hurt a change-led government, so any investment is a leadership decision.
segments.who: Six Christian-majority Galilee villages hold 27,005 eligible voters and turned out 59% in 2022, when Arab lists took 76% and change-bloc predecessors 18.5%. The model projects change lists at {{seg.arab_christian.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% in 2026, with the Democrats leading the change vote in all six. Kafar Yasif and Rame are the largest.
segments.moves: Meretz kept a foothold in Christian villages in 2022, with 11.7% against 39.8% for Hadash-Ta'al in Rudnitzky's count. Crime and personal security dominate Arab voters' concerns. The Democrats are the change list best placed to win Arab votes directly. They are touring Arab towns and expanding Arabic social media. Ra'am's leader estimates Arab support for Zionist parties at no more than 10-12%.
segments.approach: The change bloc runs no field programme here. The atlas publishes no town-level values or ranks for these villages, and the planner never includes Arab localities. At saturation the whole segment is worth about {{seg.arab_christian.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes toward a change-led government and about {{seg.arab_christian.block_nb__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} toward denying Netanyahu 61, because general turnout here adds mostly Joint List votes. The bloc runs no turnout programme here whatever the value. The Democrats' own Arabic-language campaign is that list's decision and goes through its election counsel. Any turnout support beyond it is a leadership decision and must be independent, transparent and cleared in writing by election counsel.
segments.message: Any bloc communication that reaches these villages should speak to personal security and action on crime, equal services, and respect for Arab citizens' votes.
segments.messenger: The bloc does not recruit, brief or script messengers for Arab-sector turnout work, and any independent group chooses its own. No bloc-run or bloc-branded turnout activity in these towns. A list's own campaign for its own Arab voters, such as the Democrats' Arabic-language campaign, is that list's decision and goes through its election counsel.
segments.avoid: Avoid rhetoric that treats Arab votes as illegitimate. One weak 2019 survey experiment found no Jewish backlash to centre-left equality messages aimed at Arab citizens. Even so, bloc spokespeople should not make Arab turnout a campaign theme or comment on Arab-sector turnout figures, because Likud plans to use the CEC's station turnout releases to rally its base. The bloc runs no election-day transport or other election-day turnout activity here. Election-day transport, gifts and activity near polling stations are regulated, so check with election counsel.
segments.caveat: Per 10,000 votes, the Joint List moves the chance of a change-led government by about {{mv.JL.govt|f:+.2f}} points under the formation model and the chance of denying Netanyahu 61 by about {{mv.JL.deny|f:+.2f}} points under the seat law. Any support is a leadership decision and must be independent, transparent and cleared by election counsel.

segments.role: Decisive for denying Netanyahu 61, holding about half of that objective's potential, but negative for a change-led government under the formation model. Whether to invest is a leadership decision.
segments.who: The segment's 84 Arab localities in the Galilee and the Triangle, including Ghajar, which is not targeted, hold 670,493 eligible voters. Turnout was 54% in 2022 and Arab lists took 93%. The model projects Arab lists at {{seg.arab_north_triangle.p26_arab|x100|f:.0f}}% and change lists at {{seg.arab_north_triangle.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%. Nazareth, Umm al-Fahm, Shefa-'Amr and Tayibe are the largest towns.
segments.moves: Arab turnout swings far more than Jewish turnout, from 64.8% in 2020 to 44.6% in 2021. It responds to how the Arab lists run, perceived influence, local candidates and backlash against exclusion. Crime is the top issue: about 80% rank it first in Statnet's polling, and 53.5% name it among their top two factors in IDI's August survey. About 77% back an Arab party joining the coalition. The CEC's vote to disqualify the Joint List and Ra'am, overturned unanimously by the Supreme Court on 2 October, may lift turnout.
segments.approach: Change-bloc lists run no turnout programme of their own here. The atlas publishes no town-level values or ranks for these localities and makes no recommendation on where or among whom turnout should rise. The planner never includes Arab localities. Per 10,000 extra Arab-list votes, the chance of denying Netanyahu 61 rises by about {{mv.JL.deny|f:.2f}} points for Joint List votes and {{mv.Raam.deny|f:.2f}} points for Ra'am votes under the seat law. Under the formation model the chance of a change-led government falls by about {{mv.JL.govt|abs|f:.2f}} points for Joint List votes and barely moves for Ra'am votes (about {{mv.Raam.govt|f:+.2f}}). The Strategy page's scenario engine puts a 5-point national rise in Arab turnout, about {{lev.arab_turnout_+5.votes|sig2|f:,.0f}} votes, at about {{lev.arab_turnout_+5.deny|f:+.1f}} points for denying Netanyahu 61 and about {{lev.arab_turnout_+5.govt|f:+.1f}} points for a change-led government. Under the deny-61 objective the segment holds about {{seg.arab_north_triangle.block_nb__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation. If leadership chooses to support Arab-sector turnout, that support must be independent of the bloc's campaign, transparent and cleared in writing by election counsel. Everywhere, the bloc's own job is to keep its messaging from delegitimising Arab citizens.
segments.message: The bloc's own national messaging should treat Arab citizens and their votes with respect, and speak to personal security and crime, which Arab voters rank first, and to services.
segments.messenger: The bloc does not recruit, brief or script messengers for Arab-sector turnout work, and any independent group chooses its own. A list's own campaign for its own Arab voters, such as the Democrats', is that list's decision and goes through its election counsel. National spokespeople should address Arab citizens with respect.
segments.avoid: Avoid change-bloc rhetoric that paints reliance on Arab votes as illegitimate, which can deepen alienation. Bloc spokespeople should not make Arab turnout a campaign theme or comment on Arab-sector turnout figures. Likud plans to use the CEC's station turnout releases to rally its base, echoing its 2015 election-day message about Arab turnout, and visible threat narratives mobilise the other side. No bloc-run or bloc-branded turnout activity in these towns.
segments.caveat: Arab-sector turnout is a leadership decision, and the two objectives point in opposite directions here. Any support is independent, transparent and cleared by election counsel. Funding or in-kind help for another list's or a civil-society group's turnout work raises Party Financing Law questions and, as a 2019 CEC ruling on Bedouin busing showed, can require registration as a body active in the elections. Ghajar, a restricted border village, is not targeted.

segments.role: A candidate-dependent opportunity, held out of the realistic budgets until a check of the filed CEC lists and a Druze poll. On paper it holds about {{seg.druze.change_govt__share|x100|f:.0f}}% of change-led-government potential and the best yield per contact, but it is the model's least certain projection.
segments.who: The segment's 18 Druze and Circassian localities hold 96,043 eligible voters. Turnout was 48.5% in 2022, against 77-79% in 1996-99. Change-bloc predecessors took 68% in 2022. The model projects change lists at {{seg.druze.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% after pooling each village 60% toward the segment average, because 2022 votes followed home-village candidates. Mughar (17,008 eligible) is the largest and the only one where Arab lists lead the projection. Daliyat al-Karmel, Yirka, Isfiya, Beit Jann and Kisra-Sumei project {{x.segments.druze_named_change_min|x100|f:.0f}}-{{x.segments.druze_named_change_max|x100|f:.0f}}% for change lists, a figure that depends on 2026 candidates.
segments.moves: Druze voting is utilitarian and candidate-driven. Almost every party that put a Druze candidate in a winnable slot won that candidate's home village, and kinship and Druze candidates are the strongest predictors of the Druze vote. Home-village peaks run 30-50 points above the Druze average, as with Blue and White's 78.1% in Daliyat al-Karmel in September 2019 and Meretz's 64.8% in Beit Jann in April 2019. In April 2019 a Likud candidate also moved Yirka from the Joint List to Likud. The open grievances are Kaminitz-law fines and demolitions, the planning and housing shortage, and the Nation-State Law. A 2025 university release suggested that Israel's moves to protect Druze in Sweida may pull some voters toward Netanyahu. That is commentary, not polling, and the research desk found no 2026 Druze poll.
segments.approach: Treat Druze turf as a candidate-dependent opportunity, not a headline. The realistic budgets on this site leave Druze towns out until two checks are done. First, check the filed CEC lists for which lists placed Druze candidates in winnable slots. Second, run a quick Druze poll. If both support it, these towns would add about {{x.segments.druze_add_min|sig2|f:,.0f}}-{{x.segments.druze_add_max|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes to the change-led-government budgets. Per contact they lead the map on paper: Kisra-Sumei {{loc.1296.change_govt__area_eff1k|f:.1f}}, Beit Jann {{loc.480.change_govt__area_eff1k|f:.1f}} and Daliyat al-Karmel {{loc.494.change_govt__area_eff1k|f:.1f}} net votes per 1,000 door contacts, against {{loc.5000.change_govt__area_eff1k|f:.1f}} in Tel Aviv-Yafo. Where the checks hold, run in-community supporter contact led by local Druze figures in the nine villages tiered turnout engines under the default objective: Daliyat al-Karmel, Beit Jann, Yirka, Kisra-Sumei, Yanuh-Jat, Isfiya, Julis, Mughar and Sajur. Split turf by each station's lead change list. At town level Yashar leads in Daliyat al-Karmel, Yirka, Isfiya, Kisra-Sumei and Sajur, and Yisrael Beytenu in Mughar, Julis and Yanuh-Jat. The Democrats lead Beit Jann's projection only because of a 2022 Meretz home-candidate vote, so assign that turf after the candidate check. Stations where Arab lists lead get no door or list programme: {{x.segments.arab_led_mughar}} of Mughar's 31 stations, {{x.segments.arab_led_isifya}} of Isfiya's 17 and {{x.segments.arab_led_peqiin}} of Peqi'in's 8. Work only the stations the model marks positive.
segments.message: Planning and zoning relief and equality under the Nation-State Law, using only commitments in the lists' published platforms or cleared by list leadership. Reach former Blue and White voters through media and calls to identified voters, not in the in-community contact, launched with the final published polls on Friday 23 October. Threshold arithmetic only: a list under 3.25% elects no one. On Fri 23 Oct the ask may cite the final published polls, never the atlas forecast. Friday creative that quotes a poll carries the survey details the law requires and comes down before the ban starts at the end of that day. From Sat 24 Oct quote no poll or forecast figures.
segments.messenger: Druze figures with winnable slots on the filed CEC lists, local notables and family networks. Yashar's Kamil Abu Rokon, a retired Druze general and former Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories, is a natural lead if his slot on Yashar's filed list is winnable, so check the filed list. Volunteers from the villages themselves do the contact. Send no outside volunteers.
segments.avoid: Do not message Druze villages as part of the Arab sector, and do not rely on national messaging. Do not headline Druze towns or over-invest before the candidate check, since candidate effects have swung these villages by double digits and a post-Sweida shift toward Netanyahu is an untested risk. Do not organise rides. Help supporters plan public transport or a family ride, and check any other transport help with election counsel.
segments.caveat: The Druze projection is the least certain in the model. It depends on which lists placed Druze candidates in winnable slots in 2026, and pooling only partly removes 2022 home-village votes such as Beit Jann's 62% for Meretz. A stress test that moves 20 points from change to Netanyahu-bloc lists in Druze towns changes {{x.segments.druze_stress_changed}} of the top 25 localities under the default objective. The four Golan Druze villages (Majdal Shams, Buq'ata, Mas'ade and Ein Qiniyye) are not targeted. Hurfeish and Reihaniyye sit in the Lebanon border zone, where capacity is halved. Planning note, not for scripts: the forecast gives Blue and White about {{mv.BW.share|f:.1f}}% and about a {{fc.BW.pass|x100|f:.0f}}% chance of passing.

segments.role: A Netanyahu-bloc stronghold where the bloc runs no door work. The only value is a small amount of list contact with identified change supporters.
segments.who: The segment's 28 Haredi localities hold 378,343 eligible voters, and {{x.segments.haredi_strongholds}} of the 28 are tiered Netanyahu-bloc strongholds under the default objective. Beit Shemesh is tiered supporter-list ground, because its small value, about {{loc.2610.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation, comes only from list contact. Turnout was 75% in 2022 and the Netanyahu bloc took 96%, with Modi'in Illit, Betar Illit and El'ad voting at 81-84%. Bnei Brak (115,586 eligible) and Beit Shemesh (78,064, {{loc.2610.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% projected change) are the largest. The segment also takes in mixed towns such as Netivot, Safed and Giv'at Ze'ev, where change lists project {{x.segments.haredi_mixed_change_min|x100|f:.0f}}-{{x.segments.haredi_mixed_change_max|x100|f:.0f}}%.
segments.moves: Haredi turnout is high and stable, and UTJ's vote has grown at about 95% of the pace of its electorate since 1992. In 2022, 97% of Haredi voters backed the coalition parties. Arutz Sheva reported on 6 October, citing Kan recordings, that UTJ's chairman fears lower turnout after the failed draft-exemption law. The research desk could not verify that report, so treat it as unconfirmed. A new Haredi Public list splits the vote, and Shas is losing traditional voters to Otzma, Likud and Yashar over the draft crisis.
segments.approach: Run no door canvassing and no general turnout work. The model finds no positive door turf in any station in the segment, because every extra general turnout vote here nets the Netanyahu bloc. It scales persuasion to 15% of normal, and at that level persuasion calls add nothing measurable. The segment's whole value, about {{seg.haredi.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation, comes from calls and relational asks to identified change supporters, mainly in Beit Shemesh, Safed, Bnei Brak and Netivot, plus a little from rescue calls. Yashar leads the change vote in {{x.segments.haredi_yashar_leads}} of the 28 localities, so its lists should carry this work.
segments.message: Where contact happens, talk to traditional voters about equal burden and the cost of living, with clear respect for religious life.
segments.messenger: Observant and traditional messengers known in the community. Secular change-bloc activists stay out.
segments.avoid: Avoid visible campaigning in Haredi neighbourhoods and draft rhetoric that reads as an attack on Haredim. US studies find that a visible out-group and a disliked messenger can mobilise or harden the other side. The research desk found no Israeli test of either, so treat this as a risk to manage. Never run activity aimed at lowering anyone's turnout. The Strategy page's scenario engine puts {{lev.nb_turnout_25000.votes|f:,.0f}} extra Netanyahu-bloc votes at about {{lev.nb_turnout_25000.govt|f:+.1f}} points for a change-led government.

segments.role: A Netanyahu-majority city with a large change minority, tiered a turnout engine under the default objective because door work in its positive polling stations is worth slightly more than its supporter lists. The value comes from working a minority of polling stations and contacting identified supporters, not from citywide canvassing.
segments.who: Jerusalem has 432,125 eligible voters and turned out 62% in 2022, when the Netanyahu bloc took 77% and change-bloc predecessors 20%. The model projects {{seg.jerusalem.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% change and {{seg.jerusalem.p26_nb|x100|f:.0f}}% Netanyahu bloc, with about {{seg.jerusalem.persuadable_voters|sig2|f:,.0f}} persuadable voters (a modelled figure) and about {{seg.jerusalem.rescue_voters|sig2|f:,.0f}} Blue and White or Reservists voters. Yashar leads the change vote, with the Democrats second. The city ranks fifth on the map by change-led-government potential, at about {{loc.3000.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation.
segments.moves: Turnout rose in right-wing strongholds, Jerusalem among them, in 2022. Neighbourhoods differ sharply, and the model finds positive door value in only {{x.segments.jerusalem_positive}} of the city's 706 stations. Nationally, the draft (26%) and the October 7 inquiry (22%) are decisive for young secular voters. Traditional and moderate religious voters are most likely to respond to equal burden, October 7 accountability and security competence. Among 2022 Likud voters considering a switch, October 7 (37%) and the draft (23%) are the main reasons, and 35% of religious reservists would consider not voting for a party that backs draft exemption.
segments.approach: Split the city by polling station and by list. Door work is limited to the {{x.segments.jerusalem_positive}} stations the model marks positive, where change lists project {{x.segments.jerusalem_pos_change_min|x100|f:.0f}}-{{x.segments.jerusalem_pos_change_max|x100|f:.0f}}%. At saturation it is worth slightly more than phone and relational contact citywide (about {{loc.3000.change_govt__area_pot|sig2|f:,.0f}} against {{loc.3000.change_govt__list_pot|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes). Yashar leads {{x.segments.jerusalem_pos_yashar}} of the positive stations and the Democrats {{x.segments.jerusalem_pos_democrats}}. The {{x.segments.arab_led_jerusalem}} stations where Arab lists lead get no door or list programme. Elsewhere, call and message identified change supporters, and make persuasion calls to identified soft Netanyahu-bloc voters. Jerusalem gets a door team in three of the four realistic change-led-government plans, worth about {{x.segments.jerusalem_govt_150k_0|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at 150,000 contacts without supporter lists. It rises further once supporter lists exist. At 400,000 contacts with 30% of supporters identified it is worth about {{x.segments.jerusalem_govt_400k_30|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes, fourth after Tel Aviv-Yafo, Haifa and Ramat Gan. That assumes the lists already exist. Building them takes identification contacts the plan does not count. Reach Blue and White and Reservists voters through media, digital and calls to identified voters, launched with the final published polls on Friday 23 October, not by knocking on doors. Friday creative that quotes a poll carries the survey details the law requires and comes down before the ban starts at the end of that day. From Saturday 24 October, when the poll-publication ban is in force, rescue messages and call scripts quote no poll figures, only the threshold arithmetic.
segments.message: Give traditional and moderate religious voters security competence and equal burden, framed around unity and a broad government. Give secular and young voters the draft and October 7 accountability. Give Blue and White and Reservists voters the threshold arithmetic: a list under 3.25% elects no one. Say it with respect for their reservist commitment.
segments.messenger: Right-credentialed figures such as Eisenkot and Bennett, Yashar religious-Zionist figures such as Matan Kahana, and reservists speaking as civilians. Never reach reservists through IDF units, unit chat groups, bases or employers, and never use uniforms or insignia. Left-coded branding belongs only in secular base stations.
segments.avoid: Avoid citywide turnout drives, which net Netanyahu-bloc votes at a projected {{seg.jerusalem.p26_nb|x100|f:.0f}}-{{seg.jerusalem.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}} split. Avoid any visible activity in Haredi neighbourhoods that could trigger counter-mobilisation.

segments.role: A change-bloc base: change lists lead in {{x.segments.kibbutz_change_lead}} of 256 small communities, worth about {{seg.kibbutz.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation, or {{seg.kibbutz.change_govt__share|x100|f:.0f}}% of change-led-government potential. Under the default objective {{x.segments.kibbutz_low_yield}} are tiered low yield on their own, one is a secondary target and four religious kibbutzim are Netanyahu-bloc strongholds. The work therefore runs through members' own networks and phones, not door teams.
segments.who: The segment's 256 kibbutzim hold 143,566 eligible voters. Change-bloc predecessors took 83% in 2022 and the model projects change lists at {{seg.kibbutz.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%. The Democrats lead the change vote in {{x.segments.kibbutz_lead_democrats}} kibbutzim, such as Ma'agan Michael, Yagur and Na'an, and Yashar in {{x.segments.kibbutz_lead_yashar}}, such as Giv'at Brenner and Gesher HaZiv. Turnout was 70% and stayed flat in 2022 while it rose in right-wing strongholds. Kibbutzim turn out about 4 points below localities with the same socio-economic profile.
segments.moves: October 7 hit kibbutz communities directly. Be'eri, Nir Oz and Kfar Aza were still largely displaced in September 2025, and more than 60,000 residents near the Lebanese border were evacuated. On the centre-left, 60% call this the most important election ever, so motivation is high. Contact from friends works even where turnout is already high. One large US friend-to-friend texting trial found about 8 points per message received at roughly 76% baseline turnout.
segments.approach: Use base networks, relational asks and phones. Send no door teams. No kibbutz is large enough for the realistic plans to deploy one, and most already vote at rates where the model's turnout lift per contact is a fraction of its peak. Members contact members through their own contacts and the community WhatsApp groups they belong to as individuals, and volunteers call and text identified supporters. Never use the Kibbutz Movement's, a regional council's or a kibbutz secretariat's official channels, staff, newsletters or member lists, and check any such channel with election counsel. Add a vote plan to every contact. Run turnout contact only where change lists lead. In the {{x.segments.kibbutz_nb_lead}} kibbutzim where the Netanyahu bloc leads the projection, mostly religious kibbutzim and including the four strongholds, contact identified supporters only. Coordinate by lead list: the Democrats in their {{x.segments.kibbutz_lead_democrats}}, Yashar in its {{x.segments.kibbutz_lead_yashar}} and Together in its {{x.segments.kibbutz_lead_together}}. Help displaced members plan travel to their registered polling station by public transport or a family ride, and do not organise rides. Intercity buses on routes over 15 km are free from 20:00 on Monday 26 October until service ends on election day. Israel Railways is free on election day, with tickets from station counters or machines. Confirm Monday-evening trains with the CEC. Reach the segment's {{seg.kibbutz.rescue_voters|sig2|f:,.0f}} Blue and White and Reservists voters through media and calls to identified voters, launched with the final published polls on Friday 23 October. Friday creative that quotes a poll carries the survey details the law requires and comes down before the ban starts at the end of that day. From Saturday 24 October those messages quote no poll figures, only the threshold arithmetic.
segments.message: Use competitive, high-stakes framing. The 2022 result turned on about 30,000 votes and on lists that missed the threshold. Tie the ask to October 7 accountability and equal burden.
segments.messenger: Fellow members, friends and family, plus trusted regional and movement figures speaking in a personal capacity.
segments.avoid: Do not assume the base will turn out by itself, and do not spend on persuasion. Keep change-list rivalry out of kibbutz contact, since moving votes between change lists adds almost nothing unless a list is near the threshold. The Strategy page's scenario engine puts a 0.5-point shift from Yashar to the Democrats at about zero for a change-led government.
segments.caveat: Of the 256 kibbutzim, 43 near the Gaza and Lebanese borders are flagged as displaced and have their capacity halved. Whether the CEC will open special stations for evacuees, as it did with 83 special stations in the February 2025 northern municipal elections, has not been announced in anything the research desk found. Check with the CEC this week.

segments.role: The main turnout engine, holding about {{seg.liberal_urban.change_govt__share|x100|f:.0f}}% of change-led-government potential and the top of every realistic contact plan.
segments.who: The segment's 45 secular, high-SES localities hold 1.36 million eligible voters and turned out 67% in 2022. The model projects change lists at {{seg.liberal_urban.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% against {{seg.liberal_urban.p26_nb|x100|f:.0f}}% for the Netanyahu bloc. Tel Aviv-Yafo (447,576 eligible) alone holds about {{loc.5000.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation, {{x.segments.tel_aviv_national_share|f:.0f}}% of the national total, followed by Ramat Gan, Herzliya, Kfar Saba and Givatayim. About 37,000 people who voted for change-camp lists in 2021 stayed home in 2022, based on Kolot Nodedim's flow estimates.
segments.moves: Turnout barely moved here in 2022 while it jumped in right-leaning cities. The base is motivated. Change-bloc supporters, now the opposition, say they are more certain to vote than coalition supporters (80% vs 72%), and an N12 analysis puts the bloc's target above 76% turnout among its supporters in the Sharon, Tel Aviv and Haifa. Nationally, the draft (26%) and the October 7 inquiry (22%) are decisive for young secular voters. The segment also holds the largest pool of Blue and White and Reservists voters on the map, about {{seg.liberal_urban.rescue_voters|sig2|f:,.0f}}.
segments.approach: Choose turf station by station. The model marks {{x.segments.liberal_positive|f:,.0f}} of the segment's 2,235 stations positive. The {{x.segments.arab_led_tel_aviv}} Tel Aviv-Yafo stations where Arab lists lead get no door or list programme. Among towns with 5,000 or more voters, Tel Aviv-Yafo has the best door efficiency outside the Druze villages, at {{loc.5000.change_govt__area_eff1k|f:.1f}} net votes per 1,000 contacts. Among the segment's other towns of that size, Kiryat Tiv'on ({{loc.2300.change_govt__area_eff1k|f:.1f}}), Givatayim ({{loc.6300.change_govt__area_eff1k|f:.1f}}), Caesarea ({{loc.1167.change_govt__area_eff1k|f:.1f}}), Herzliya ({{loc.6400.change_govt__area_eff1k|f:.1f}}), Ramat Gan ({{loc.8600.change_govt__area_eff1k|f:.1f}}) and Ramat HaSharon ({{loc.2650.change_govt__area_eff1k|f:.1f}}) come next. Tel Aviv-Yafo tops every realistic plan, with about {{x.segments.tel_aviv_govt_150k_0|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at 150,000 contacts even without supporter lists. Assign each station to its lead change list. Yashar leads most positive stations, the Democrats lead about two in five of Tel Aviv-Yafo's ({{x.segments.tel_aviv_pos_democrats}} of {{x.segments.tel_aviv_positive}}), and Together is the usual runner-up elsewhere. Where a station's lead list cannot staff it, the locality's lead list takes it, or the locality's runner-up if that is the same list. Yashar's own campaign avoids Tel Aviv, so the four field directors should agree the station map, including who covers Tel Aviv-Yafo, by Thursday 15 October. Lists share the station map and aggregate counts only. Share no voter-level records unless election counsel clears the format in writing, and clear any spending that helps another list with both lists' counsel and treasurers. Concentrate live contact in the last 7-10 days through doors, volunteer phones and relational texting, with a vote plan in every conversation. Send identified supporters one or two SMS reminders 1-3 days before 27 October, in a format confirmed with election counsel and never referring to anyone's voting history. Segmented texts count as direct mail under the Privacy Protection Law, so each must say so, name the database controller and the data source, and offer removal from the list. Remind supporters registered at another address, often their parents', that intercity buses on routes over 15 km are free from 20:00 on Monday 26 October and that Israel Railways is free on election day. Confirm Monday-evening trains with the CEC. Reach Blue and White and Reservists voters through media, digital ads and calls to identified voters, launched with the final published polls on Friday 23 October. Friday creative that quotes a poll carries the survey details the law requires and comes down before the ban starts at the end of that day. From Saturday 24 October those messages and call scripts quote no poll figures, only the threshold arithmetic.
segments.message: Use competitive framing. Meretz missed the threshold by about 4,000 votes in 2022, and the Netanyahu bloc came out ahead by about 30,000. For Blue and White and Reservists voters, state the threshold arithmetic only, and with respect: a list under 3.25% elects no one. On Fri 23 Oct the ask may cite the final published polls, never the atlas forecast. Friday creative that quotes a poll carries the survey details the law requires and comes down before the ban starts at the end of that day. From Sat 24 Oct quote no poll or forecast figures.
segments.messenger: Volunteers, and above all friends and family through relational asks. Each list's activists lead in the stations where their list leads. Reservists are the right messengers to voters of the reservist-branded, right-of-centre Reservists list, and they speak as civilians. Never reach reservists through IDF units, unit chat groups, bases or employers, and never use uniforms or insignia.
segments.avoid: Avoid public boasts about high turnout, which Likud plans to use to rally its base, and 'vote for the biggest party' appeals, which helped sink Meretz in 2022. Do not chase raw low turnout in emigrant-heavy areas, where many registered voters now live abroad. Do not send door teams after Blue and White or Reservists voters, who make up about {{x.segments.national_rescue_share|f:.0f}}% of a station's voters. Door conversations carry turnout and persuasion only.
segments.caveat: Station rankings may still favour stations whose low 2022 turnout reflects residents who moved or emigrated, because the model applies one abroad share per locality, so check walk lists against local knowledge. Rescue value is positive under the default objective. For Reservists voters it turns negative under the deny-61 objective, because a Reservists vote already counts against a Netanyahu 61 if the list passes, and the model sends 40% of rescued voters to Likud. Plan totals carry wide ranges. The 150,000-contact plan without supporter lists is worth about {{bud.govt.150k.0.ve|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes, with a range of about {{bud.govt.150k.0.lo|sig2|f:,.0f}}-{{bud.govt.150k.0.hi|sig2|f:,.0f}} across assumption sets. Planning note, not for scripts: the forecast puts Blue and White at about {{mv.BW.share|f:.1f}}% (about a {{fc.BW.pass|x100|f:.0f}}% chance of passing) and the Reservists at about {{mv.Reservists.share|f:.1f}}% (about a {{fc.Reservists.pass|x100|f:.0f}}% chance). Published polls split by house. Maariv, Channel 16, Kantar and Zman Yisrael had the Reservists at 4-5 seats from late September. Channel 12 and Channel 14 gave them 4 seats on 12 October. Channel 13, i24 and Kan's 4 October poll had them below the line. A survey experiment abroad, probably in Sweden, suggests that threshold-insurance appeals work mainly when polls show a list just below the line. Our judgement is that a rescue appeal to their voters is likely to work only if Friday's final polls show them below it. The Strategy page weighs the Blue and White and Reservists options.

segments.role: A secondary target where the change-led-government value sits in a few polling stations and in supporter lists. Stations where Arab lists lead get no door or list programme, and Arab neighbourhoods follow the same leadership rule as the Arab segments.
segments.who: Five mixed Jewish-Arab cities and the village of Neve Shalom hold 219,177 eligible voters and turned out 60% in 2022, when the Netanyahu bloc took 56%, Arab lists 21% and change-bloc predecessors 21%. Lod (58,888 eligible) and Ramla (57,383) project {{loc.7000.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% change against {{x.segments.lod_ramla_nb_min|x100|f:.0f}}-{{x.segments.lod_ramla_nb_max|x100|f:.0f}}% for the Netanyahu bloc, while Nof HaGalil ({{loc.1061.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% vs {{loc.1061.p26_nb|x100|f:.0f}}%) and Ma'alot-Tarshiha ({{loc.1063.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% vs {{loc.1063.p26_nb|x100|f:.0f}}%) are closer. Yashar leads the citywide change vote in Lod and Ramla, and Yisrael Beytenu in Akko, Nof HaGalil and Ma'alot-Tarshiha.
segments.moves: The Russian-speaking Jewish neighbourhoods of Nof HaGalil and Ma'alot-Tarshiha are Yisrael Beytenu ground. In 2022 Balad was strongest among Arab voters in Lod, and Hadash-Ta'al in Akko and Nof HaGalil. Those parties now run together in the Joint List. Crime dominates Arab voters' concerns, while Jewish voters weigh security and the cost of living most.
segments.approach: Work strictly at polling-station level. Stations where Arab lists lead get no door or list programme. The model marks {{x.segments.mixed_city_positive}} stations positive: {{x.segments.lod_positive}} of Lod's 103, where change lists project {{x.segments.lod_pos_change_min|x100|f:.0f}}-{{x.segments.lod_pos_change_max|x100|f:.0f}}%, {{x.segments.maalot_positive}} in Ma'alot-Tarshiha, {{x.segments.nof_hagalil_positive}} in Nof HaGalil, {{x.segments.akko_positive}} in Akko and {{x.segments.ramla_positive}} in Ramla. Under the default objective, run selective door work only in Lod's {{x.segments.lod_positive}} positive stations. Lod is the only mixed city that gets a door team in the realistic plans, and only at 400,000 contacts. Reach the positive stations in Ma'alot-Tarshiha, Nof HaGalil, Akko and Ramla by calls to identified supporters. Yisrael Beytenu leads the change vote in {{x.segments.mixed_city_pos_yb}} of the {{x.segments.mixed_city_positive}}, including all {{x.segments.lod_positive}} in Lod and all {{x.segments.nof_hagalil_positive}} in Nof HaGalil, so its volunteers should lead this turf, with Yashar taking the other eight. Most of the segment's value, about {{seg.mixed_city.change_govt__list_pot|sig2|f:,.0f}} of {{seg.mixed_city.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation, comes from calls to identified change supporters and persuasion calls to identified soft Netanyahu-bloc voters in stations where Arab lists do not lead. Staff polling committees and observers fully within CEC rules. Since the High Court's 17 September ruling they may not report which identifiable voters have voted. Put vote-protection staff in stations with large change-bloc vote counts, stations where change lists have no committee member, and stations with past irregularity complaints.
segments.message: Personal security, crime and the cost of living for everyone. For Russian-speaking voters, add religion-and-state fairness, including civil marriage and equal burden in the draft.
segments.messenger: Russian-speaking Yisrael Beytenu activists, speaking Russian to older voters, and local Jewish community figures for persuasion.
segments.avoid: Avoid citywide turnout drives, which net Netanyahu-bloc votes in Lod and Ramla. Avoid material that sets Jewish and Arab residents against each other, since visible group-threat narratives mobilise the other side.
segments.caveat: Turnout in the Arab neighbourhoods carries the same objective trade-off as the Arab segments. The atlas makes no recommendation there. It is a leadership decision, and any support must be independent, transparent and cleared by election counsel.

segments.role: Middle Israel's big swing cities, holding about {{seg.mixed_urban.change_govt__share|x100|f:.0f}}% of change-led-government potential, where turnout and persuasion both pay and station selection decides which to use.
segments.who: The segment's 14 large central and coastal cities hold 982,973 eligible voters and turned out 66% in 2022. The model projects a narrow change lead, {{seg.mixed_urban.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% against {{seg.mixed_urban.p26_nb|x100|f:.0f}}% for the Netanyahu bloc, with about {{seg.mixed_urban.persuadable_voters|sig2|f:,.0f}} persuadable voters (a modelled figure) and about {{seg.mixed_urban.rescue_voters|sig2|f:,.0f}} Blue and White or Reservists voters. Under the default objective Haifa (about {{loc.4000.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation), Rishon LeZion ({{loc.8300.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}}) and Rehovot ({{loc.8400.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}}) are turnout engines, and Petah Tikva ({{loc.7900.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}}) is the map's only persuasion battleground.
segments.moves: Rehovot, Petah Tikva, Haifa and Rosh HaAyin are among the cities that track the national result most closely, and pluralities flip here, as in Rishon LeZion and Rosh HaAyin in 2019-20 when Likud mobilised its voters. The swing voters are traditional non-religious and secular Likud voters. The traditional non-religious split 46% Likud to about 31% Yesh Atid and National Unity in 2022. Voters who place themselves in the centre name the economy (40.5%) and the draft (34%) among their top two factors, and undecided voters want cost-of-living relief and less polarisation. Yashar is campaigning along the Route 4 suburbs, Petah Tikva and Rishon LeZion among them.
segments.approach: Split each city by polling station. Run door work in the stations the model marks positive: {{x.segments.rishon_positive}} of Rishon LeZion's 344, {{x.segments.haifa_positive}} of Haifa's 424, {{x.segments.petah_tikva_positive}} of Petah Tikva's 320 and {{x.segments.rehovot_positive}} of Rehovot's 182. Haifa's {{x.segments.arab_led_haifa}} stations where Arab lists lead get no door or list programme. Rishon LeZion has the largest persuasion value on the map (about {{loc.8300.change_govt__pers_pot|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation), and Petah Tikva is the only town where persuasion is the larger mechanism (about {{loc.7900.change_govt__pers_pot|sig2|f:,.0f}} of {{loc.7900.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}}). Hold persuasion conversations there and in balanced stations elsewhere, and make persuasion calls to identified soft Netanyahu-bloc voters where door work would net the other side. Haifa is second only to Tel Aviv-Yafo in every realistic plan. Yashar leads most positive stations and should lead the turf, with Yisrael Beytenu taking the {{x.segments.haifa_pos_yb}} positive Haifa stations it leads and Together as the usual runner-up. Message-test soft-right framings online before paid spend, and put paid media into the final 5-7 days. Reach Blue and White and Reservists voters through media and calls to identified voters, launched with the final published polls on Friday 23 October. Friday creative that quotes a poll carries the survey details the law requires and comes down before the ban starts at the end of that day. From Saturday 24 October those messages quote no poll figures, only the threshold arithmetic. In politically mixed households, limit turnout contact to confirmed supporters, since a UK field experiment found that partisan turnout appeals spread to other household members.
segments.message: Lead with competence, cost of living and equal burden in the draft, framed around unity and a broad government that includes the centre-right. US survey experiments found that voters are more persuadable about candidates they know less about, and that more informative messages persuade more. An Italian field experiment found that messages about a candidate's competence and record won more votes than ideological ones. So put Eisenkot's and Bennett's records ahead of attacks on Netanyahu, whom every voter already knows.
segments.messenger: Right-credentialed messengers such as Eisenkot, Bennett and Liberman, and reservists speaking as civilians, for soft-right voters. Never reach reservists through IDF units, unit chat groups, bases or employers, and never use uniforms or insignia. At the door, use neighbours and local volunteers rather than candidates.
segments.avoid: Avoid untargeted turnout work in Likud-leaning neighbourhoods, which Likud's own drive targets and where extra turnout nets Netanyahu-bloc votes. Keep left-coded messengers out of persuasion turf.

segments.role: Hundreds of small, mostly change-leaning communities worth about {{seg.moshav_rural.change_govt__share|x100|f:.0f}}% of change-led-government potential. They are too small and scattered for door teams, so the work runs through base networks, relational asks and phones.
segments.who: The segment's 458 moshavim and rural communities hold 251,812 eligible voters and turned out 73% in 2022. Change lists project {{seg.moshav_rural.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% against {{seg.moshav_rural.p26_nb|x100|f:.0f}}% for the Netanyahu bloc, and Yashar leads the change vote in {{x.segments.moshav_lead_yashar}} of them. The segment splits sharply, from Kfar Vitkin ({{loc.190.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% projected change) and Giv'at Ela ({{loc.1288.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%) to Sha'ar Efraim ({{loc.661.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%) and Shetulim ({{loc.763.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%). Under the default objective {{x.segments.moshav_low_yield}} are tiered low yield, because each is too small for door teams, and {{x.segments.moshav_strongholds}} are Netanyahu-bloc strongholds.
segments.moves: Education, religiosity and income sort these communities more than ethnic origin does. Traditional and right-leaning moshavim are open to the draft wedge, since 60% of reservists who fought in the war would consider not voting for a party that backs exemption, including 48% of right-wing reservists. The segment holds about {{seg.moshav_rural.rescue_voters|sig2|f:,.0f}} Blue and White and Reservists voters. Soldiers' and reservists' double-envelope votes are counted centrally, so home turnout understates real turnout in some communities.
segments.approach: Use base networks: phone and relational contact through members' own contacts and community WhatsApp groups, plus calls and texts to identified supporters. Never use local committees', regional councils' or moshav associations' official channels, staff or resident lists, and check any such channel with election counsel. Send no door teams. No moshav is large enough for the realistic plans to send one, and driving between small communities is costly. Run turnout contact only in change-leaning communities. In balanced traditional moshavim, make persuasion calls to identified soft Netanyahu-bloc voters. Yashar leads the change vote in {{x.segments.moshav_lead_yashar}} of the 458 communities, the Democrats in {{x.segments.moshav_lead_democrats}} and Yisrael Beytenu in one. Each list calls its own identified supporters in the communities it leads. Lists share the community map and aggregate counts only, share no voter-level records without written counsel clearance, and clear any spending that helps another list with both lists' counsel and treasurers. Reach Blue and White and Reservists voters through media and calls to identified voters, launched with the final published polls on Friday 23 October, not through door visits. Friday creative that quotes a poll carries the survey details the law requires and comes down before the ban starts at the end of that day. From Saturday 24 October those messages quote no poll figures, only the threshold arithmetic.
segments.message: Equal burden in the draft and reserve duty, security competence and the cost of living. For Blue and White and Reservists voters, the threshold arithmetic, put with respect for their service.
segments.messenger: Neighbours and community members, local council members speaking in a personal capacity, and reservists from the community speaking as civilians. Never reach reservists through IDF units, unit chat groups, bases or employers, and never use uniforms or insignia.
segments.avoid: Do not run turnout work in the {{x.segments.moshav_nb_majority}} moshavim and rural communities where the Netanyahu bloc projects a majority. Do not read low home turnout in soldier-heavy communities as headroom.
segments.caveat: Of the 458 communities, 32 near the Lebanese and Gaza borders are flagged as displaced, with capacity halved. Check where residents are living now before planning contact.

segments.role: Netanyahu-majority cities with large change minorities. Value comes mostly from calling identified supporters and making persuasion calls to identified soft Netanyahu-bloc voters, while untargeted turnout work nets Netanyahu-bloc votes and feeds Likud's own drive.
segments.who: The segment's 33 Likud-leaning cities and development towns hold 1.25 million eligible voters and turned out 63% in 2022. The Netanyahu bloc projects {{seg.periphery_likud.p26_nb|x100|f:.0f}}% against {{seg.periphery_likud.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% for change lists. The segment holds the most persuadable voters on the map (about {{seg.periphery_likud.persuadable_voters|sig2|f:,.0f}}, a modelled figure) and {{seg.periphery_likud.change_govt__share|x100|f:.0f}}% of change-led-government potential (about {{seg.periphery_likud.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation), more of it from supporter lists than from door work. Under the default objective Netanya, Be'er Sheva and Eilat are supporter-list ground, Holon is a turnout engine, and Tiberias and Dimona are Netanyahu-bloc strongholds. Kiryat Motzkin ({{loc.8200.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% change) and Kiryat Bialik ({{loc.9500.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%) are among the few places where change lists lead.
segments.moves: Only 58% of 2022 Likud voters said in May they would definitely vote Likud again, and those considering a switch cite October 7 (37%) and the draft (23%). Shas is losing traditional voters to Otzma, Likud and Yashar, and 65% of northern residents say the state is abandoning the north. Likud's own drive targets low-turnout stations where it won about half the vote on about 35% turnout, which it values at 2-3 seats. A joint Likud-RZP programme ranks stronghold neighbourhoods by turnout and Likud share.
segments.approach: Lead with supporter lists. Identify change supporters first, then call, text and use relational asks to get them out, because door canvassing nets Netanyahu-bloc votes in most stations here. If 30% of supporters are already identified, Netanya and Be'er Sheva rise near the top of the realistic plans, at about {{x.segments.netanya_govt_150k_30|sig2|f:,.0f}} and {{x.segments.beer_sheva_govt_150k_30|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at 150,000 contacts. That assumes the lists exist. Building them takes identification contacts the plan does not count. Make persuasion calls to identified soft Likud and traditional voters with message-tested scripts. The model scores them at 0.3% switching per call. Send door teams only to stations the model marks positive. That means {{x.segments.holon_positive}} of Holon's 259, most of Kiryat Motzkin's and Kiryat Bialik's, {{x.segments.netanya_positive}} of Netanya's 319, {{x.segments.beer_sheva_positive}} of Be'er Sheva's 283 and {{x.segments.eilat_positive}} of Eilat's 85. Tiberias has only one of 65, too few for a door team. In the supporter-list towns, phone and relational contact is the main channel and door work stays within their positive stations. Yashar leads the change vote throughout and leads the contact, using its local organisers in towns such as Dimona to call its own identified voters (no door work in strongholds). Yisrael Beytenu takes the stations it leads. Lists share the station map and aggregate counts only, with no voter-level records unless counsel clears it in writing. Reach Blue and White and Reservists voters through media and calls to identified voters, launched with the final published polls on Friday 23 October. Friday creative that quotes a poll carries the survey details the law requires and comes down before the ban starts at the end of that day. From Saturday 24 October those messages quote no poll figures, only the threshold arithmetic.
segments.message: Lead with October 7 accountability, security competence and equal burden in the draft, with respect for voters' past Likud loyalty. More voters trust an Eisenkot-led government than Netanyahu to fix the October 7 failures (48% vs 30%). Add local themes of neglect, rebuilding and jobs.
segments.messenger: Right-credentialed messengers, including Eisenkot and Yashar's local organisers, Liberman for Russian-speaking residents, reservists speaking as civilians, and trusted local figures. Never reach reservists through IDF units, unit chat groups, bases or employers, and never use uniforms or insignia. Volunteers rather than candidates should knock on doors, and Russian-speaking and Mizrahi communities in the same town need separate messages and messengers.
segments.avoid: Avoid generic turnout drives, which net Netanyahu-bloc votes here and help Likud's Golden Clusters programme. Avoid attacks on Netanyahu or Likud voters, which harden his supporters. Do not read very low turnout in places like central Eilat or Netanya's hotel strip as headroom, since it likely reflects non-resident registration.
segments.caveat: Eilat's raw 2022 turnout (43%) is distorted by people registered there who do not live there, so the model applies a phantom-roll correction and its Eilat figures carry extra uncertainty. Kiryat Shmona, Shlomi and Sderot are flagged as displaced border towns with capacity halved. Between about 40% and 60% of Kiryat Shmona's residents had not returned by August-September 2026, depending on the report.

segments.role: A Netanyahu-bloc stronghold with one narrow persuasion opening among moderate religious-Zionists in mixed suburbs, best served by Yashar's existing operation.
segments.who: The segment's 103 religious-Zionist communities inside the Green Line hold 77,462 eligible voters. Turnout was 77% in 2022 and the Netanyahu bloc took 82%. Under the default objective {{x.segments.rz_strongholds}} of the 103 are Netanyahu-bloc strongholds. Giv'at Shmuel (20,150 eligible, {{loc.681.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% projected change) is the only secondary target, while Yad Binyamin, Nof Ayalon and Bareqet project {{x.segments.rz_named_change_min|x100|f:.0f}}-{{x.segments.rz_named_change_max|x100|f:.0f}}% change.
segments.moves: Religious-Zionist voters moved right between 2019 and 2022. An early-September Dialog poll put Yashar and Together at about 7% combined in the sector, with security (35%) and Jewish identity (25%) ahead of the draft (15%). Yashar aims for about two more seats from traditional and moderate religious-Zionist voters through a headquarters under Matan Kahana covering Gush Etzion, Efrat, Giv'at Shmuel and Ariel. Among religious reservists, 35% would consider not voting for a party that backs draft exemption.
segments.approach: Run no turnout work. The segment's door value is about {{seg.religious_zionist.change_govt__area_pot|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes, mostly in {{x.segments.givat_shmuel_positive}} of Giv'at Shmuel's 33 stations, and none of the realistic plans sends a door team there. The model scales persuasion to 60% of normal here and the whole segment holds about {{seg.religious_zionist.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation, so keep the investment small. Let Yashar's religious-Zionist operation make persuasion calls to identified moderates in Giv'at Shmuel and in mixed communities such as Hosha'aya. Any staff, call-centre or paid volunteer costs another list puts into that operation need prior written clearance from both lists' election counsel and treasurers. Coordinate so the change lists do not duplicate effort. Yashar leads the change vote in {{x.segments.rz_lead_yashar}} communities, Giv'at Shmuel among them, and Together in {{x.segments.rz_lead_together}}, such as Yad Binyamin and Nof Ayalon.
segments.message: Security competence, shared service and equal burden, and respect for Jewish identity, framed around a broad national government.
segments.messenger: Religious-Zionist figures such as Matan Kahana, religious reservists speaking as civilians, and local community members. Never reach reservists through IDF units, unit chat groups, bases or employers, and never use uniforms or insignia.
segments.avoid: Avoid secular or left-coded messengers and religion-and-state attacks that read as hostile to religious life. Run no turnout work.

segments.role: Netanyahu-leaning cities with large Russian-speaking communities, where Yisrael Beytenu carries much of the bloc's case and the value is split between selected door turf, supporter lists and persuasion.
segments.who: The segment's 10 Russian-speaking towns hold 580,965 eligible voters and turned out 59% in 2022. The Netanyahu bloc projects {{seg.russian_speaking.p26_nb|x100|f:.0f}}% against {{seg.russian_speaking.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% for change lists. The segment holds about {{seg.russian_speaking.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation, roughly {{x.segments.russian_gotv_share|f:.0f}}% from turnout, {{x.segments.russian_pers_share|f:.0f}}% from persuasion and {{x.segments.russian_resc_share|f:.0f}}% from rescue calls. Under the default objective Ashdod (181,784 eligible, {{loc.70.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% change) and Bat Yam (51% turnout, {{loc.6200.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% change) are turnout engines, and Karmiel ({{loc.1139.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%) and Nesher ({{loc.2500.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%) lean to the change lists.
segments.moves: Russian speakers are about 15% of the population and 50-60% secular. Adult 1990s immigrants lean right, those who arrived as teenagers lean centrist, and the Israeli-born generation votes like other Israelis. Likud voters are split on religion-and-state questions such as civil marriage. Yisrael Beytenu has mapped the neighbourhoods and polling stations where Likud did best and is concentrating on Russian-speaking ex-Likud voters. The research desk found no 2026 poll of Russian speakers, so the model leans on past results.
segments.approach: Work at polling-station level. Ashdod and Bat Yam are turnout engines under the default objective, so send door teams to their positive stations ({{x.segments.ashdod_positive}} of Ashdod's 302, {{x.segments.bat_yam_positive}} of Bat Yam's 211) and add calls to identified supporters. Bat Yam gets a door team even in the 150,000-contact plan without supporter lists, and Ashdod in the 400,000-contact plans. Send door teams to the positive stations of Ashkelon ({{x.segments.ashkelon_positive}} of 198) and most of Karmiel's, Nesher's, Kiryat Yam's and Arad's. Make persuasion calls to identified ex-Likud voters in Likud-leaning stations of Ashdod and Ashkelon. Split turf by lead list. Yisrael Beytenu leads almost half of Ashdod's positive stations ({{x.segments.ashdod_pos_yb}} of {{x.segments.ashdod_positive}}), about a third of Bat Yam's ({{x.segments.bat_yam_pos_yb}} of {{x.segments.bat_yam_positive}}) and {{x.segments.ashkelon_pos_yb}} of Ashkelon's {{x.segments.ashkelon_positive}}. It also leads the citywide change vote in Kiryat Yam, Migdal HaEmek, Arad and Bnei Ayish. Yashar leads the rest. Contact older and 1990s-immigrant voters in Russian through Russian-speaking volunteers, and keep separate messages and messengers for the Mizrahi and Russian-speaking communities of the same town.
segments.message: Religion-and-state fairness, including civil marriage and equal burden in the draft, plus security competence and the cost of living.
segments.messenger: Liberman and Yisrael Beytenu's Russian-speaking activists, Russian-language media and community figures.
segments.avoid: Avoid Hebrew-only material for older voters, and untargeted turnout work in Ashdod and Ashkelon, where the Netanyahu bloc projects {{x.segments.ashdod_ashkelon_nb_min|x100|f:.0f}}-{{x.segments.ashdod_ashkelon_nb_max|x100|f:.0f}}%. Discount raw low turnout. It may partly reflect emigration and an older population rather than voters who can be mobilised.
segments.caveat: The model's data predate immigrants who arrived from Russia and Ukraine after 2022, so newer Russian-speaking voters are not reflected in these projections.

segments.role: A Netanyahu-bloc stronghold with no field work beyond Yashar's existing religious-Zionist outreach.
segments.who: The segment's 83 national-religious West Bank settlements hold 102,322 eligible voters. Turnout was 75% in 2022 and the Netanyahu bloc took 91%. The model projects {{seg.settlement_rz.p26_nb|x100|f:.0f}}% for the Netanyahu bloc and {{seg.settlement_rz.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% for change lists, and {{x.segments.settlement_rz_strongholds}} of the 83 are Netanyahu-bloc strongholds under the default objective. Efrat (7,945 eligible, {{loc.3650.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% projected change) is the largest, and Bet El ({{loc.3574.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%) and Kiryat Arba ({{loc.3611.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%) are the least open of the larger settlements.
segments.moves: RZP took about 60% of the vote east of the separation barrier in 2022, and security and Jewish identity lead the sector's concerns. Yashar's Kahana-led headquarters covers Efrat and Gush Etzion. Soldiers' double-envelope votes are counted away from home, and adding them back lifts Judea and Samaria turnout by about 10 points, so recorded turnout understates real turnout.
segments.approach: Run no turnout work and no change-bloc field operation. The model finds almost no positive door turf ({{x.segments.settlement_rz_positive}} of 197 stations), and the segment's whole value is about {{seg.settlement_rz.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation, from list contact. Leave the narrow opening in Efrat and Gush Etzion to Yashar's religious-Zionist team, using phone and relational contact with identified moderates. Coordinate with Together, which leads the change vote in {{x.segments.settlement_rz_lead_together}} of the 83 settlements, including Efrat, Bet El and Elkana. Share only the community map and aggregate counts. Share no voter-level records without written counsel clearance. Any staff or call costs that help another list need clearance from both lists' counsel and treasurers.
segments.message: Security competence, equal burden and a broad national government that respects religious life.
segments.messenger: Religious-Zionist figures and local residents connected to Yashar's operation.
segments.avoid: Avoid visible secular campaigning, which can provoke counter-mobilisation. Never treat low recorded turnout as headroom.

segments.role: A low-yield segment of secular and mixed West Bank localities, where what little value there is comes from persuasion in Ariel and Ma'ale Adumim and from a few change-leaning communities near the Green Line.
segments.who: The segment's 32 secular and mixed West Bank localities hold 78,737 eligible voters and turned out 70% in 2022. The Netanyahu bloc projects {{seg.settlement_secular.p26_nb|x100|f:.0f}}% against {{seg.settlement_secular.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% for change lists. Ma'ale Adumim (28,142 eligible, {{loc.3616.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}% change) and Ariel ({{loc.3570.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%) are the largest, while Kfar HaOranim ({{loc.3796.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%), Har Adar ({{loc.3769.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%), Oranit ({{loc.3760.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%) and Alfei Menashe ({{loc.3750.p26_change|x100|f:.0f}}%) lean to the change lists.
segments.moves: The Netanyahu bloc took 63% here in 2022, and Yisrael Beytenu leads the change vote in Ariel. Yashar's religious-Zionist headquarters covers Ariel. The draft is a strong wedge with right-leaning reservist communities, since 48% of right-wing reservists would consider not voting for a party that backs exemption.
segments.approach: Keep the effort small. The whole segment holds about {{seg.settlement_secular.change_govt__potential|sig2|f:,.0f}} net votes at saturation, and persuasion supplies most of it (about {{seg.settlement_secular.change_govt__pers_pot|sig2|f:,.0f}}). Make persuasion calls to identified soft Netanyahu-bloc voters in Ariel, where Yisrael Beytenu leads, and in Ma'ale Adumim, where Yashar leads. Oranit and Alfei Menashe, where Yashar leads every station, are tiered low yield, so reach their supporters by phone and relational contact, not door teams. The model values them mainly for persuasion. Rescue stays with media and calls to identified voters. Reach Har Adar and Kfar HaOranim through relational contact.
segments.message: Security competence, equal burden in the draft and reserve duty, and the cost of living.
segments.messenger: Yisrael Beytenu and Yashar local activists, reservists speaking as civilians, and residents. Never reach reservists through IDF units, unit chat groups, bases or employers, and never use uniforms or insignia.
segments.avoid: Avoid citywide turnout work in Ariel and Ma'ale Adumim, where the Netanyahu bloc projects {{x.segments.ariel_maale_nb_min|x100|f:.0f}}-{{x.segments.ariel_maale_nb_max|x100|f:.0f}}%. Do not read low home turnout in soldier-heavy communities as headroom.
